notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, as reported to the Auditor of Public Accounts from the locality's audited financial statements, not a budget.
Towns sit inside counties, and town residents pay both. Warren County runs the schools and most other services, so the town's budget is small next to the county's.
Covers general government, capital projects, debt service (principal and interest) and enterprise activities such as water, sewer and electric utilities. Depreciation is left out.
Left out: borrowing ($0), non-revenue receipts ($65,699) and transfers between the locality's own funds.
Non-departmental spending and capital projects other than schools and roads ($573,939) are spread across departments in proportion to their size.
Judicial administration (courts, the Commonwealth's attorney and clerks) and community development count as overhead.
Debt is gross debt at year end: bonds, Literary Fund loans, other long-term obligations and temporary loans, for general government and enterprise activities.
Political money is not scored: no local candidate committee could be placed in this locality.

Cameras: 8 license-plate cameras are mapped inside Town of Front Royal's borders in OpenStreetMap (8 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Virginia yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

Transparency: Town of Front Royal has filed its comparative cost report with the Auditor of Public Accounts for FY 2025, the latest year most VA governments have filed. This is a check that the report was filed, not an opinion on its contents. The other five practices have not been checked yet, so they are left out of the score.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 8 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside Town of Front Royal's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
